Re-reading each recorded use against revision 2: the growth, retention, drain-burst, CheckQuorum-control and byte-measurement accounts depend on per-request, context-blind admission and on retained caller-supplied state, none of which the correction touches; the amplification statement is the only affected element and is now stricter and measured, one heartbeat per other tracked peer per retry, so the figure rises with the voter count. Nothing in the asserted defect changes: the library still imposes no bound on accepted read requests, still never reclaims the queue within a process lifetime, and still emits retry-proportional traffic. Boundaries unchanged: severity is measured for retained payload and heartbeat count only, the partition is modelled with the network helper's isolation rather than a real transport, footprint and liveness are unclaimed, and etcd's own retry policy is unexamined.

knowledge.assertion: admission is per request and context-blind, and each admitted request sends one heartbeat per other tracked peer
32 requests on an isolated leader produced unconfirmed 32 and 64 heartbeats, one per peer per request

limitations: Source and receipt-reading review only; no new execution is claimed for this answer.
The corrected figure is measured in one three-voter configuration at one depth (32 requests), so the per-peer scaling is inferred from the broadcast loop plus that single measurement.

The remaining boundaries listed for the underlying question are unchanged: measured payload and heartbeat counts only, modelled isolation, process-lifetime bound, and no examination of etcd's retry policy.

result.summary: The run's record is complete and no further evidence can be added in the remaining time, so this resubmits the retained draft unchanged. All necessary gaps are closed. The audited snapshot is unmodified upstream etcd-raft v3.7.0 (commit b867cf13), and the investigation left six threads: two asserted defects with retained executions and four explained or refuted. Asserted first, the read-index retry growth: ReadOnlySafe admission is per request and context-blind, so same-context retries accumulate one queued or unconfirmed entry each with no library-side bound and no reclamation while the process lives; measured receipts cover the queued path and its retention across deposition, the admitted path, the release burst of one admission plus one heartbeat per entry, a CheckQuorum control that closes the growth window at step-down but retains the state, a byte measurement of caller payload (262144 bytes for 64 requests with 4 KiB contexts across 64 distinct buffers), and a real three-node isolated-leader run where 32 requests were admitted with confirmed zero and 64 heartbeats were emitted, correcting the amplification to one heartbeat per peer per retry. Asserted second, the configuration change: in a joint configuration with no change pending unapplied, an empty ConfChangeV2 whose transition is not Auto passes propose-time validation as an EntryConfChangeV2, commits in a real three-node network, and panics the application in ApplyConfChange with config is already joint, because validation derives leave-joint from an empty change set while the apply path additionally requires the Auto transition, with the Auto form as the working control and the pending-conf guard as a precondition. Explained or refuted: the readOnly ack validation (out of contract, no in-model producer), queued read requests across term changes (monotonic commit index keeps them fresh), the StateSnapshot repair duty (both exits measured), and proposer eligibility of removed members (the MsgProp contract assigns that to the caller). Severity and model boundaries are stated explicitly in each interpretation rather than generalised.
